original_test_intent: Verify that every Type 20 Memory Array Mapped Address Handle resolves uniquely to the correct Type 19 range and that this range owns the referenced Type 17 device within the intended Type 16 array before and after reboot.
original_method: Collect complete raw Type 16/17/19/20 tables, resolve each Type 20 array-range handle to exactly one Type 19 structure, check that its device range is contained and its Type 19 array points to the expected Type 16 owner, and repeat after approved reboot.
manual_activity: A user supplies the array/range/device graph and approves reboot; no physical or mapping action is intrinsic.
required_inputs: Expected Type 16 arrays and Type 19 mapped ranges
Expected Type 17 devices and Type 20 range ownership
Complete relationship parser and read-only OS-map context
safety_requirements: Use read-only collection; do not change DIMMs, firmware, kernel or memory maps.
Require each Type 20 array handle to resolve to exactly one Type 19 record and retain the complete range/device context.
Never silently replace orphan, duplicate, reserved or wrong-owner references.
Require reboot approval/recovery; stop on graph drift or boot failure and do not auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Build the Type 16/17/19/20 relationship graph, resolve every Type 20 array handle, validate containment and ownership, and compare pre/post reboot.
Report orphan, duplicate, wrong-parent, out-of-range or drifting relations without issuing PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve expected topology and special interleaved/disabled/vendor exceptions plus reboot plan.
Resolve relationship conflicts and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The field label is correct, but grep cannot prove unique Type 19 resolution, Type 16 ownership or that the Type 20 device range belongs to it.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive full raw Type 16/17/19/20 data; report every Type 20-to-Type 19 resolution, referenced ranges/devices, Type 16 owner, containment and pre/post graph diff.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The array-mapped handle scope, script and 5/5-minute values are retained; no mapping repair is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve each Type 20 array-range handle uniquely to Type 19, follow that range to Type 16 ownership and the Type 20 device to Type 17, validate containment/approved exceptions, and compare after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, firmware and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 16/17/19/20 handle and mapped-range definitions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds unique Type 19 resolution and end-to-end array/range/device graph validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects dangling, duplicated, wrong-array or range-inconsistent references missed by a handle grep.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved topology graph and exception policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Interleaved/logical mappings can be valid but must be explicitly modeled; OS-map correlation cannot repair a broken SMBIOS reference.

project_override_considerations: A project may define multiple arrays, interleaving and disabled memory, but each Type 20 reference must still follow a documented unique Type 19-to-Type 16 ownership path.
expected_evidence: Approved Type 16/17/19/20 topology and exception policy
Complete pre-reboot raw tables with versions/lengths
Unique Type 20-to-Type 19 resolution table with device range, Type 17 identity and Type 16 owner
Approved reboot/health evidence and post-reboot graph diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Memory Array Mapped Address Handle is a valid Type 20 cross-reference; topology is a project input.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Unique resolution, containment and graph persistence are automatable after inputs.
